paragraphs: Many children with disabilities in Libya cannot go to normal schools because the schools don’t have money or special teachers. Because of this, many children stay at home and feel very sad or lonely.

In 2020, a woman and her mother started a small family center to help them. The center is in a town near the capital city, Tripoli. Every day, more than 40 children and teenagers come there to learn how to read, write, and speak. Other private schools are very expensive, but this center helps poor families and costs very little money.

Parents are very happy with the results. One 6-year-old girl with Down syndrome couldn’t speak before and used to cry and scream. Now, she can talk clearly, tell her family how she feels, and she is much happier.

words.d: when a person cannot do things which other people can easily do
controlled by one person or a small group, not by the government

paragraphs: In Libya, many children with special problems cannot go to school. Normal schools do not have good teachers for them. So, these children stay at home and are very sad.

A kind woman and her mother open a small center in 2020 to help these children. More than 40 children go there every day. They learn how to read, write, and talk. Other centers cost a lot of money. This place is very cheap. It helps poor families.
The children’s lives are changing. One small girl cannot speak before. She is very upset. Now, she can talk to her mom and dad, and she smiles a lot. The center gives these children a happy life.

words.d: when something costs very little money
when you have very little money

paragraphs: In Libya, many children with special needs and learning disabilities are left outside the public school system because regular schools lack trained staff and proper resources.

To change this, two women opened a private center called Elim in 2020. Located about 80 kilometers from Tripoli, the center helps more than 40 children and teenagers every day with individual lessons, and it focuses on learning difficulties and speech problems. While other private centers in the capital are far too expensive for ordinary people, Elim supports low-income families by charging only a very small, token fee. Parents say the center makes a huge difference; without this support, many children suffer from depression and social anxiety because they cannot communicate.

For example, a 6-year-old girl with Down syndrome couldn’t speak and used to scream out of frustration. Today, after attending the sessions, she can speak clearly and express her feelings, which has made her confident and happy.

words.d: a very small amount of money that you pay for something, just to show a rule or support, not a real price
a strong feeling of worry, fear, or nervousness about what might happen
the feeling of being annoyed, angry, or disappointed because you cannot do what you want to do
